native_reference.description: rex-env-bench (crates/rex-env/src/bin/bench.rs), release build, dm3.bsp, the same start/goal pair used throughout this evidence file, deterministic pseudo-random policy (hold-forward + view sweep + jump pulses).

remeasured_today.note: Median of 3 repeats today (140.85 M/s) is within 1% of the spec's stated 139.5 M/s figure; used the spec's 139.5 M/s as the comparison baseline below since that is the number the spec names, with today's remeasurement recorded here as independent confirmation it still holds.

python_boundary.description: PyVecEnv.step() through the full PyO3 + numpy boundary: dm3.bsp, Route::planned(start, goal) (a real navmesh route, not Route::new's straight line), a trivial random policy (uniform noise over (fwd, side, dyaw, jump), regenerated fresh every single step() call so numpy's own generation cost is inside the timed loop) -- the environment plus the boundary and nothing else, no torch, no learned policy.
python_boundary.methodology: 5 repeats per N, each repeat: warmup calls (~10% of the timed count, to pay for rayon thread-pool spin-up once, off the clock) then a timed loop of step() calls with a freshly-generated (N,4) float32 action array each call; reported rate is env-steps (N * calls) / wall time. Median of 5 repeats reported below; full per-repeat spread in raw_results.

finding: The retained fraction is poor -- 2.15% at N=1024, plateauing around 4.6-4.9% by N=4096-16384 -- and does not recover materially with more N in this range, unlike a per-step-FFI-call design (which the spec already rules out) where batching alone would be expected to keep buying throughput roughly linearly with N. Isolating the cost (env.step() called with a PRE-generated action array, i.e. excluding numpy's own random-generation cost, at N=16384: ~2.06ms/call versus a pure-compute estimate of ~117us if 16384 env-steps split evenly across 64 threads at the native per-step cost) shows the gap is dominated by per-call parallel-dispatch overhead, not environment or array-marshalling cost: VecEnv::step() opens a fresh rayon par_iter_mut() region on every single Python-level step() call, so every call pays for waking/redistributing work across the (idle between calls) thread pool and joining at the end, rather than rayon's worker threads ever running in a tight loop the way rex-env-bench's threads do (each of rex-env-bench's 64 std::thread::spawn threads loops millions of ticks internally and is never parked between them). That per-call wake/join tax does not shrink as N grows, so it dominates at these batch sizes and the retained fraction stays in the low single-digit percent instead of approaching 100%. This is reported as a design finding per the spec's instruction, not quietly tuned around: the two fixes the spec names are a bigger N (partial relief only -- the fraction is already flattening out by N=16384) or moving the policy into Rust so the per-tick loop never crosses the Python boundary at all (this is what rex-selfplay / a live rollout loop would do for real training throughput; PyVecEnv is for phase-1 debugging/inspection from Python, not for burning through tens of millions of RL steps).

build_and_import.why_a_feature_flag: pyo3/numpy are optional deps gated behind the `python` Cargo feature so a plain `cargo build`/`cargo test -p rex-env` (and every other crate in the workspace) never needs a Python interpreter or pulls in pyo3.
build_and_import.import_setup: CPython resolves an extension module by exact filename (module name + `sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')`), so the cdylib is exposed to the target venv by symlinking it under that name into the venv's site-packages: ln -sf $(pwd)/rtx/target/release/librex_env.so /home/benjamin-adm/rex-ml/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/rex_env.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so -- a symlink rather than a copy so a rebuild is picked up without re-copying. No maturin/pip involved (neither is installed in that venv); this venv's python (a uv-managed venv) is the same /usr/bin/python3.12 pyo3's build script auto-detected, so no ABI mismatch.
build_and_import.verified_import: /home/benjamin-adm/rex-ml/.venv/bin/python -c "import rex_env; env = rex_env.PyVecEnv(bsp_path, start, goal, n); obs = env.reset(); obs, parts, dones = env.step(actions)"
